story.title: Tricky Riddles
story.midCtaText: Enjoying the quiz? Subscribe & hit the bell!
story.subscribeText: New quiz every day – turn on the bell 🔔

questions.q: You overtake the runner in **2nd place**. Your place now?
Which is heavier: a **kilo** of feathers or a kilo of bricks?
How many animals of each kind did **Moses** take on the ark?
A ship's ladder: 3 rungs underwater. The **tide** rises 1 m. Now?
If **yesterday** was Thursday, what is the day after tomorrow?
2 people paint 2 walls in 2 hours. **4 people**, 4 hours?
Odd number: drop **one letter** and I'm even. Which?
A clock strikes **6** in 5 seconds. How long to strike 12?
No siblings: "His father is my **father's son**." Who?

lines.q: Ten tricky riddles, and they get harder every round, so keep score! Round one, easy. You overtake the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
lines.a: Second! You took their spot, not the leader's.

lines.q: Which is heavier? A kilo of feathers, or a kilo of bricks?
lines.a: Neither! A kilo is a kilo. The bricks just hurt more if you drop them.

lines.q: How many animals of each kind did Moses take on the ark?
lines.a: None! It was Noah's ark, not Moses. Nice and easy so far?

lines.q: Round two, medium. A rope ladder hangs over the side of a ship, with three rungs underwater. The tide rises one metre. How many rungs are underwater now?
lines.a: Still three! The ship floats, so it rises with the tide.

lines.q: What comes next? Two, five, ten, seventeen, twenty six...
lines.a: Thirty seven! The gaps grow by two each time. Three, five, seven, nine, eleven. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: If yesterday was Thursday, what is the day after tomorrow?
lines.a: Sunday! Today is Friday, tomorrow is Saturday. How many have you got so far?

lines.q: Round three, hard. Two people paint two walls in two hours. How many walls do four people paint in four hours?
lines.a: Eight! Twice the people, twice the time. Two times two times two. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: I'm an odd number. Take away one letter, and I become even. Which number am I?
lines.a: Seven! Drop the S, and you get even. Sneaky, right?

lines.q: Final round, legend. A clock takes five seconds to strike six. How long does it take to strike twelve?
lines.a: Eleven seconds! Six strikes have five gaps, one second each. Twelve strikes have eleven gaps.

lines.q: Final question. A man with no brothers or sisters points at a photo and says: that man's father is my father's son. Who is in the photo?
lines.a: His son! My father's son is me, so that man's father is me.
